newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - Eurobourses end mixed, uncertain on US data.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Eurobourses end mixed, uncertain on US data.

text.p: European bourses were mostly down at the close of trade on Friday in an uncertain response to U.S. economic figures showing few inflationary pressures but a slowing economy.

On currency markets, the dollar ended the European day slightly stronger against the mark but showing a loss on the yen after remarks by a senior German central banker supporting the Japanese currency.

The U.S. figures gave some smaller bourses a lift but London, Europe's biggest, failed to be aroused from interest rate worries prompted by data on Britain's economic performance in October which registered an 18-month high.

Wall Street itself, which closed strongly on Thursday, made an unsteady opening after the release of the U.S. figures showing the unemployment rate was unchanged at 5.2 percent in October, suggesting few inflationary presssures.
This picture of a slowing economy was confirmed by later data which said the U.S. manufacturing sector grew more sluggishly in October than in September.
The data, according to Roy Blumberg, chief investment strategist at Josephthal Lyon, showed "no inflation pressures. That's bond market heaven."

Investors would normally judge lower inflation as auguring well for lower interest rates, good for business. But Blumberg noted that a slowing economy, even absent inflationary pressures, did not bode well for corporate profits.

London's FTSE index closed down 0.8 percent. Investors had taken fright as a stronger-than-expected purchasing managers index, an important guide to Britain's economic performance, raised prospects of more harsh medicine after Wednesday's shock interest rate increase.

Frankfurt floor trading, which ended before the U.S. figures came out, closed up nearly one percent. Computerised dealing, however, ended in the minus column market after a day of thin trading. Swiss shares ended up but below the levels reached on release of the U.S. figures. Amsterdam was up nearly one percent at the close of trading.
The dollar closed mixed in European trading, edging lower against the yen but holding on to some of its gains against the mark.
The long-awaited U.S. jobs figures gave only a short-lived nudge higher to the dollar since they were in line with expectations and hourly earnings, a measure of wage inflation, were flat.
"There wasn't much in those numbers to push the dollar either way," said Jeremy Stretch, currency strategist at NatWest Markets in London.
The mark fell against the yen after Bundesbank council member Ernst Welteke said a strong yen against the mark would help German exporters.

"The latest pattern is simply to trade off the latest comment you see on the screen -- and the last comment was Welteke's," said David Coleman, chief economist at CIBC Wood Gundy. "Basically he was talking the deutschemark down."
CURRENCIES
The dollar was trading around 1.5145 marks and 113.15 yen in late European trading versus 1.5132 and 113.77 on Thursday.
STOCKS CLOSING PRICES
The Financial Times-Stock Exchange index of 100 leading British shares ended 30.6 points lower at 3,948.5.
In Paris the CAC-40 was closed for a Market holiday. at last trade the share index finished up 15.75 at 2,140.51.
The 30-share DAX index in Frankfurt closed up 24.0 at 2,683.25. PRECIOUS METALS
Gold closed at $377.65 an ounce, compared to Thursday's close of $379.75. Silver ended off eight cents at $4.78.
